title: End-to-End Probabilistic Framework for Learning with Hard Constraints
claim: Our constrained probabilistic method is faster than the baseline and gives well-calibrated uncertainty across linear, nonlinear and inequality constraint types.
layout: 3 panels in a row, each labeled by constraint type, shared caption
description: Three side-by-side plots, each titled by a constraint type. Panel (a), Linear Equality: Timing, is a grouped bar chart of time per iteration in seconds across five time-series datasets (Labour, Tourism, Wiki, Traffic, Tourism-L). Green and blue bars are the two ProbHardE2E variants and red bars are the HierE2E baseline. The red bars are much taller, and the gap grows on the larger datasets. Panels (b) Nonlinear Equality: PME and (c) Convex Inequality: TVD are line plots of u(x,t) against x, zoomed in on a propagating front. Each has a thick black true solution curve and several colored mean curves with shaded ±3σ uncertainty bands in red, blue and purple. The eye goes first to the tall red bars, then to the shaded bands around the sharp step.
caption: \ourmethod{} on the various constraint types. (a) Linear Equality: Average time per iteration (in seconds) for \ourmethod{}, compared to the HierE2E on five hierarchical time-series datasets; (b) Nonlinear Equality: Mean $\pm$3 standard deviation for the PME with conservation constraint at time $t=0.51$, with PDE parameter $m_{train}\in[3,4]$ and $m_{test}=3.88$; (c) Convex Inequality: Mean $\pm$3 standard deviation for linear advection with TVD constraint at time $t=0.51$, with PDE parameter $\beta_{train} \in [1,2]$ and $\beta_{test} = 1.5$. The horizontal axes in (b)-(c) are zoomed in to highlight the uncertainty near the propagating front.
abstract: We present ProbHardE2E, a probabilistic forecasting framework that incorporates hard operational/physical constraints, and provides uncertainty quantification. Our methodology uses a novel differentiable probabilistic projection layer (DPPL) that can be combined with a wide range of neural network architectures. DPPL allows the model to learn the system in an end-to-end manner, compared to other approaches where constraints are satisfied either through a post-processing step or at inference. ProbHardE2E optimizes a strictly proper scoring rule, without making any distributional assumptions on the target, which enables it to obtain robust distributional estimates (in contrast to existing approaches that generally optimize likelihood-based objectives, which are heavily biased by their distributional assumptions and model choices); and it can incorporate a range of non-linear constraints (increasing the power of modeling and flexibility). We apply ProbHardE2E in learning partial differential equations with uncertainty estimates and to probabilistic time-series forecasting, showcasing it as a broadly applicable general framework that connects these seemingly disparate domains.
